scope: Stage 0 planning only; no PBIR, TMDL, or theme implementation

confirmed: One imported table named RetailSales is present.
The workbook contains 60 rows and OrderID is unique across all 60 rows.
The observed row grain is one order per row; there is no confirmed order-line grain.
OrderDate spans 2026-01-01 through 2026-05-28 with 50 distinct dates.
StoreName has 3 values, Region 2, ProductName 8, Category 4, CustomerID 10, PaymentMethod 3, and OrderStatus 2.
All observed source columns are complete with no nulls.
current_gaps: OrderDate is currently typed as Int64 in TMDL although the source workbook exposes datetime values; this must be resolved in Stage 1.
No date dimension or dedicated store/product dimensions are present.
unknowns: Business currency is UNKNOWN; use a neutral currency/number format until confirmed.
The meaning of Returned is UNKNOWN beyond the source status value; do not infer whether sales/profit should be reversed.
The discount field's unit is UNKNOWN beyond integer values 0, 5, and 10; validate whether it represents percent points.

proposed_pages.title: Retail Performance Overview
proposed_pages.purpose: Leadership scan of sales, profit, order volume, return rate, store contribution, and recent trend.

proposed_pages.title: Store and Category Performance
proposed_pages.purpose: Compare store, region, category, and product contribution to identify performance concentration.

proposed_pages.title: Sales Trend and Mix
proposed_pages.purpose: Analyze monthly sales/profit movement and the mix of completed versus returned orders and payment methods.

proposed_pages.title: Order Detail
proposed_pages.purpose: Provide a filterable order-level operational view for investigation.

navigation.placement: below the page title/header and above the analytical canvas
navigation.consistency: same order, dimensions, typography, active-state treatment, and spacing on every page
navigation.interaction: page navigation buttons or tabs; active page uses Simplifica primary color and inactive pages use neutral text

theme_strategy: Use themes/0. Simplifica.json as the required source of truth in Stage 2. Do not replace it with the current Fluent base theme. Preserve its palette and white background, then add only implementation-safe text, visual, slicer, and navigation defaults needed by the approved design contract.

static: Confirm every visual id is unique
Confirm every position is within 1920x1080 and uses 8px-aligned coordinates
Confirm no visual overlaps within a page
Confirm every field binding exists in the Stage 1 model contract
pbir: Run powerbi-report-author validate against the .Report directory after each Stage 2/3 logical batch
Review warnings as well as failures
desktop: Open/reload the PBIP in Power BI Desktop
Refresh and verify no model errors
Capture screenshots for all four pages
render: Review desktop screenshots at FitToPage and a narrow viewport
Check navigation, slicers, clipping, labels, contrast, and table readability
final_qa: Reconcile Total Orders, Total Sales, Total Profit, Units Sold, and Returned Orders to source workbook calculations
Confirm no currency assumption was introduced

hitl_checkpoints: Approve the interpretation of one row per OrderID and the OrderDate type correction before Stage 1.
Confirm business currency and whether Returned orders remain included in sales/profit totals.
Approve the four-page structure, top navigation, and Simplifica theme usage before Stage 2.
Review the first rendered desktop screenshots before final QA.
technical_acceptance_criteria: Stage 0 artifacts describe the actual Retail Store model, not the prior defect model.
No PBIP, PBIR, TMDL, or theme files are modified in Stage 0.
All planned fields and measures are either observed in the current model or explicitly marked as Stage 1 additions.
Every planned visual has a page, purpose, type, binding, filters/sorting where relevant, and in-bounds layout coordinates.
The required Simplifica theme is preserved as the source of truth.
Unknown business semantics are recorded as UNKNOWN rather than guessed.
